output.headline: Pays National Equity Project up to $4,800 for equity-focused staff training courses

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $4,800.00

output.summary: National Equity Project will teach professional learning courses to the counseling department's CAR Team, including Liberatory Design for Equity, Designing & Facilitating Meetings, Coaching for Equity and Attending to Healing. The district may pay up to $4,800 for August 8, 2022 through June 30, 2023. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays an Arabic translator and interpreter up to $18,825 through the Office of Equity

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $18,825.00

output.summary: An individual contractor will provide translation and interpretation for the district's growing Arabic-speaking population. The district may pay up to $18,825 for January 2 through May 31, 2023. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $5,000 for Safety Patrol support at Acorn Woodland Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00

output.summary: Oakland Public Education Fund will supervise and support the Safety Patrol Team at Acorn Woodland Elementary School to make the school safer and easier to reach, including safer routes to and from campus. The district may pay up to $5,000 for January 3 through May 26, 2023. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $13,000 to train people who serve Latina girls and young women

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $13,000.00

output.summary: An individual consultant will lead collaborative planning and program development, and train the adults who work with youth, to improve educational outcomes for Latina girls and young women in the district. The district may pay up to $13,000 for February 1 through May 31, 2023. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Proclaims March 19-25, 2023 as Oakland Adult & Career Education Week
output.summary: The board adopts Resolution No. 2223-0015, which proclaims March 19-25, 2023 as Oakland Adult & Career Education Week. The proclamation has no cost to the district.

output.headline: Pays National College Resources Foundation up to $15,000 to bring HBCUs to Oakland college fairs

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $15,000.00

output.summary: National College Resources Foundation will work with the High School Linked Learning Office, the NAACP and Oakland Promise to bring at least 20 Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) to host two college fairs. Students who qualify may be offered scholarships and admission on the spot, and the partners will host an awards ceremony. The district may pay up to $15,000 for November 1, 2022 through February 5, 2023. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $40,000 for McCampbell Analytical to lab-test suspect building materials

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $40,000.00

output.summary: McCampbell Analytical will test samples of suspect building material in a lab to find risks that could affect students and staff. The contract covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, for up to $40,000. The board is approving it after the fact (ratification).

output.headline: Ratifies up to $15,000 for SCA Environmental to reduce environmental risk at school sites

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $15,000.00

output.summary: SCA Environmental will provide environmental services to reduce risk at school sites, including collecting environmental samples. The contract covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, for up to $15,000. The board is approving it after the fact (ratification).

output.headline: Ratifies up to $70,000 to keep defibrillators serviced and provide a district physician

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $70,000.00

output.summary: Medical Business Professional Services Group will keep checking the defibrillators (AEDs) at district buildings and campuses, replace batteries and pads, and maintain emergency medical supplies. It will also update labor law posters and provide a physician to District Health Services for prescriptions such as Epi-Pens and medical advice. The contract covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, for up to $70,000. The board is approving it after the fact (ratification).

vendor.name: Medical Business Professional Services Group, Inc.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $60,000 for Restoration Management Company to clean up environmental hazards at sites

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $60,000.00

output.summary: Restoration Management Company will provide environmental cleanup services, as needed, to reduce risk at district school sites and properties. The contract covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023, for up to $60,000. The board is approving it after the fact (ratification).

output.headline: Pays Center for Transformative Teacher Training up to $21,000 to coach Lockwood STEAM's school leader

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $21,000.00

output.summary: The Center for Transformative Teacher Training will provide real-time leadership coaching to the school leader at Lockwood STEAM Academy, to help build learning communities with lasting results. The district may pay up to $21,000 for January 1 through June 30, 2023. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays 1Direction up to $30,000 for attendance and behavior case management at Lockwood STEAM

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $30,000.00

output.summary: 1Direction will provide case management for Tier 2 students at Lockwood STEAM Academy who need extra support with attendance and behavior. The district may pay up to $30,000 for January 1 through June 30, 2023. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost climate justice youth leadership program from Frontline Catalysts at United for Success
output.summary: Frontline Catalysts will run a three-phase youth leadership program (engage, explore, empower) grounded in ethnic studies at United for Success Academy. Students build skills while learning about climate change in their own communities and climate justice through community activism. It will not cost the district anything, and runs November 1, 2022 through May 25, 2023. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays an Arabic translator and interpreter up to $19,500 through the Office of Equity

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $19,500.00

output.summary: An individual contractor will provide translation and interpretation for the district's growing Arabic-speaking population. The district may pay up to $19,500 for January 2 through May 31, 2023. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Music Is Extraordinary up to $10,000 for an instrumental music residency at United for Success Academy

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00

output.summary: Music Is Extraordinary will provide 48 hours of instrumental music teaching during the school day at United for Success Academy, working alongside the school's music teacher and its music students. The district may pay up to $10,000 for March 13 through June 1, 2023. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Living Jazz up to $22,500 for 30 weeks of music and choir classes at Cleveland Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $22,500.00

output.summary: Living Jazz will teach music and choir to third graders during the school day at Cleveland Elementary School, covering ear training, vocal and rhythm skills, harmony and performance, and ending with a school assembly performance. The district may pay up to $22,500 for September 15, 2022 through June 30, 2023. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Pays a video producer up to $4,000 for Kwanzaa and African American Honor Roll videos

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $4,000.00

output.summary: An individual contractor will film, edit and produce videos for Kwanzaa and the African American Honor Roll for the Office of Equity. The district may pay up to $4,000 for February 1 through May 26, 2023. The service period began before the board's vote.

output.headline: Reappoints a member to the Measure G1 teacher retention oversight commission for two more years
output.summary: The board is asked to ratify the Board President's reappointment of Shae'Onna Muhammad to a second term on the Measure G1 Districtwide Teacher Retention and Middle School Improvement Act Oversight Commission. The term runs April 16, 2023 through April 15, 2025.

output.headline: Approves the minutes of the board's March 22, 2023 regular meeting
output.summary: The board is asked to approve the written minutes of its regular meeting held March 22, 2023, which staff prepared shortly after the meeting.

output.headline: Approves the minutes of the board's March 29, 2023 special meeting
output.summary: The board is asked to approve the written minutes of its special meeting held March 29, 2023, which staff prepared shortly after the meeting.

output.headline: Adopts the district's positions on 13 state bills, supporting 9 and opposing 4
output.summary: The board takes positions on 13 proposed state bills in six areas: student achievement, educator workforce, charter schools, facilities, early childhood education and governance. It supports nine (one with amendments) and opposes four, including one it opposes unless amended.

output.headline: Confirms a new member of the board's Budget and Finance Committee through January 2024
output.summary: The board is asked to ratify the Board President's appointment of Jennifer Brouhard as a member of the Budget and Finance Committee. The appointment is effective immediately and the term ends January 8, 2024.
